# Lock content presentation delegates to the pane, like reload

## Context

Operator direction 2026-09-01 on the shipped lock action (`#17949`): start with disabling, enhance later — and make the content half easy to override per widget, the way `reload` already is. A downstream product needs "locked" to mean **read-only** for the pane's content (nested forms disabled, grid cell editing off), which a blanket inert body cannot express: inert also takes away scrolling and text selection, and the primitives own their own read-only semantics.

Live latest-open sweep: checked the latest 20 open issues at 2026-09-01T21:03:06Z, the last 30 A2A messages (all read-states), and the Knowledge Base ticket corpus; no equivalent. `#17949` (merged) is the inert default this ticket keeps as the fallback.

## The Problem

- The engine has no cascading read-only axis: only `form.field.Text` and the Monaco wrapper declare a `readOnly` config; nothing propagates it, and grid cell editing has no switch. Building that cascade is a large, separate project.
- A pane author already knows what "locked" means for their content — a form container disables its fields, a grid turns cell editing off, a stream keeps scrolling. The engine cannot know, and inert is the honest blunt default when nobody tells it.
- The lock presentation today is engine-owned end to end (`Workspace#syncDockLockItemPresentation`): `pane.vdom.inert = true` with a WeakMap snapshot of prior inert ownership, plus the `neo-dock-pane-locked` class (`cursor: not-allowed` + a hairline inset outline, `resources/scss/src/dashboard/Container.scss`). There is no seam for the pane to take over.

## The Architectural Reality

- The delegation precedent is `reload` (`#17948` / `#17966`): `Workspace#syncDockReloadAction` probes `typeof pane.dockReload` on the live card — or its config's `module` prototype before the slot materializes — never a resolver call; `handleDockReloadAction` delegates to `pane.dockReload()` and otherwise runs the engine fallback.
- Structural protection is separate from content presentation and stays engine-owned: `setItemLocked` fails `closeItem` / `detachItem` / source moves closed in the reducer, the close action hides, drag sources are suppressed (`#17949` layered guards). This ticket touches only the content half.
- The revealed rail pane goes through the same presentation sync (`Workspace#syncDockLockRails` → `syncDockLockItemPresentation`), so the seam must serve both the in-flow card and the reveal overlay's pane.
- The locked-pane cursor rule currently keys on the class; the DOM `inert` attribute is the truthful discriminator between the engine default and a delegated pane.

## The Fix

1. **The hook:** a pane implementing `dockLock(locked: Boolean): void` owns what lock means for its content. `syncDockLockItemPresentation` probes it exactly like reload (`typeof` on the live card, else on the config module prototype); when present it calls `pane.dockLock(locked)` on every transition and writes no `inert` — the pane restores its own state on `dockLock(false)`. Absent hook → today's inert default, unchanged byte for byte.
2. **The visual cue splits along the truth:** `neo-dock-pane-locked` (the hairline frame) stays for both paths; `cursor: not-allowed` moves onto `.neo-dock-pane-locked[inert]`, so a read-only delegated pane does not show a forbidding cursor over content the user may scroll and select.
3. **Both surfaces:** the in-flow card and the revealed rail pane resolve the hook the same way; unlock reverses both.
4. **Docs:** the `enableDockLockAction` config JSDoc on `Workspace` carries the hook contract (mirroring the `enableDockReloadAction` wording); one pane example in the dock-lock component fixture.
5. **Witnesses:** unit (`test/playwright/unit/dashboard/DockLockAction.spec.mjs`): a pane with `dockLock` receives `true` then `false`, never gains `inert`; a pane without keeps the inert path and the exact-restore clause. Component (`test/playwright/component/dashboard/DockLock.spec.mjs`): a fixture pane whose `dockLock` disables a nested field — the field reads disabled while locked, enabled after unlock, and the pane body stays scrollable/selectable throughout.

## Contract Ledger

| Target surface | Source of authority | Proposed behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pane.dockLock(locked)` (new pane hook) | `Workspace#syncDockLockItemPresentation` | delegated content presentation on lock and unlock; engine writes no `inert` | absent → inert default with exact restore (unchanged) | `enableDockLockAction` JSDoc | unit + component witnesses |
| `.neo-dock-pane-locked[inert]` cursor rule | `resources/scss/src/dashboard/Container.scss` | `not-allowed` only for the engine-inert default | delegated panes keep the frame cue and a normal cursor | SCSS comment | component computed-style check |

**Decision Record impact:** aligned-with ADR 0029 §2.6 (container contract for embedded product surfaces: the pane stays an ordinary component the host talks to through explicit hooks).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A pane implementing `dockLock` is called with `true` on lock and `false` on unlock, on the in-flow card and on the revealed rail pane, and never receives an engine `inert` write.
- [ ] A pane without the hook keeps today's behavior exactly: inert while locked, prior inert ownership/value restored on unlock (the `#17949` exact-restore witness stays green).
- [ ] Structural protections are unaffected by the hook: close hidden, drag sources suppressed, reducer rejections on `closeItem` / `detachItem` / source moves.
- [ ] `cursor: not-allowed` applies only while the pane root carries the `inert` attribute; a delegated locked pane shows the frame cue with a normal cursor.
- [ ] The probe is pure: `typeof` on the live card or its config module prototype, no resolver call (mirrors `syncDockReloadAction`).
- [ ] The Workspace JSDoc documents the hook next to the reload delegation contract.

## Out of Scope

- A cascading read-only axis in the component tree, and per-primitive read-only semantics (form containers, grid cell editing, drag sources) — those are what a pane's `dockLock` implementation calls into; they are not minted here.
- Changing the structural half of lock or its default-off flag.
- Any consumer-specific read-only implementation.

## Avoided Traps

- **A generic `readOnly` sweep over descendants** — it would need every primitive to agree on one config, handle children added later, and still guess wrong on buttons whose handlers mutate; the pane author knows, the engine does not.
- **Keeping `inert` beside a delegating pane** — double ownership of the same DOM state is exactly what the WeakMap snapshot exists to avoid; delegation means the engine writes nothing.
